objections.claim: The spec's premise is that reporting is "a pure function of the run directory plus a handful of facts" and that the renderer has "a fixed section list and no free-text heading path." But several render rules require *interpreting* data whose schema the spec never establishes, forcing the renderer to contain exactly the kind of ad-hoc prose-derived logic the ticket exists to remove.
objections.evidence: `facts.ground_truth` is defined as "step 11.5's `faff reconcile --json` stdout, verbatim" (SummaryFacts record), yet row A19 requires the renderer to count divergences, classify each as `phantom-merge` / `claimed-shipped-unmerged` / `unowned-sibling-mutation` / `superseded-unproven` / `sibling-check-unproven`, and switch warn vs ESCALATED off `ledger.level`. That classification cannot come from rendering a blob verbatim; it needs a defined reconcile-JSON contract the spec never states. The same gap recurs: `park_records: [Object]` "verbatim" must still yield per-issue "parked N runs same root cause: [class]" lines (A13); the holdout file's schema is unspecified while A18 demands splitting `needs_human_reasons` into environment-gap vs human-only subsets; `supersession.json`'s shape is unspecified while A11 must cite "the delivering ids". The builder must invent each contract, and nothing pins it — the next change to `faff reconcile`'s output silently changes summary sections.
objections.predicted_consequence: The renderer ships with embedded parsers for four undocumented formats; the first upstream change to any of them produces a silently wrong or silently empty summary section with exit 0, and the "no free-text path" guarantee is already false in the code.
objections.disposition_rationale: Fixed in round-1 revision: input contracts table and reconcile contract test, clock-free Duration, format field, neutralised fact text, error-exit tests (park comment 37169370).

objections.claim: The renderer's safety property (A24 — "no banned heading appears", and more generally the fixed section list) is stated over the *section list*, but the spec populates the document by interpolating arbitrary fact fields — `issues[].title`, `gloss`, `routed_out[].detail`, `reasons[]`, `follow_ups[]`, `discovered_scope[].text`, `methodology.findings[]` — as free text. Any fact string containing a line beginning with `## ` (or `Deferred:`/`Queued for next run:` inside a heading position) manufactures a heading the fixed section list was supposed to make impossible. The writer of the facts file is the orchestrator agent, which the spec does establish, so this is not an authority boundary problem; but a malformed or prompt-influenced facts payload (issue titles and glosses originate in tracker content, which is untrusted third-party data flowing through the orchestrator into facts) can spoof a section heading in a document the skill then posts to the tracker as the run's authoritative record. The holdout test only covers the committed fixtures, so a real run with a hostile title passes the spec's tests and still emits the banned heading.
objections.evidence: §4.1 "An id appearing in the ledger but missing from `facts.issues` renders as `- <ID>`"; `SummaryFacts` free-text fields (gloss, detail, inferred, evidence, follow_ups, findings); A24 and the holdout "output MUST contain no heading matching 'Deferred'…"; §4.2 the skill "posts and prints what `run summary` returns".
objections.predicted_consequence: a tracker post of the run summary containing a spoofed `## Deferred`/`## Queued for next run` heading fabricated from a tracker-authored issue title, defeating A24's invariant on real runs while the fixture-only holdout stays green.
